From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 9:12 AM PT
Subject: Platform scope + resourcing: audit logging 100% sensitive-action coverage

Team — aligning scope + resourcing for the audit logging “100% sensitive action coverage” push. I want to confirm owners, expected staffing, and release gates so we’re not negotiating at the end.

Proposed workstreams / ownership (for Feb–Apr window):

1) Canonical schema + taxonomy + libraries
- Owner: Marcus (exec), Naomi (product)
- Eng: Security Eng (1.0 FTE), Platform support (0.5 FTE)
- Deliverables: schema v1 JSON Schema, event_type registry, validation helpers, redaction guidance
- Linear: ENG-4821, ENG-4822

2) Control plane: RBAC + credentials + policy/routing changes
- Owner: Platform org (under Platform)
- Eng: 2.0 FTE (Control plane)
- Deliverables: emit events on all sensitive endpoints; correlation IDs; tests
- Linear: ENG-4823, ENG-4830

3) API gateway: admin endpoints + quota overrides
- Owner: Platform org (Gateway)
- Eng: 1.0 FTE (Gateway)
- Linear: ENG-4824

4) Console/admin actions
- Owner: Console team (dependency)
- Eng: 1.0 FTE (Console backend) + 0.5 FTE (UI validation)
- Linear: ENG-4825, ENG-4837

5) Private: installer/upgrade/rollback/config apply parity
- Owner: Vivek (product)
- Eng: Private deployments team (1.0 FTE)
- Deliverables: parity coverage + operator identity where available
- Linear: ENG-4826

6) Exporter normalization + schema_version tagging
- Owner: Security Eng
- Eng: Exporter (1.0 FTE)
- Linear: ENG-4827

7) Verification: coverage dashboard + CI enforcement + E2E tests
- Owner: Platform (dashboards), Security Eng (enforcement)
- Eng: 1.0 FTE telemetry/dashboards, 0.5 FTE CI/lints, 0.5 FTE E2E
- Linear: ENG-4828, ENG-4831, ENG-4834

Cross-team dependencies we need to acknowledge up front:
- Console team must land audited admin workflows (RBAC edits, export config changes, retention settings) before we can claim 100%.
- Exporter normalization needs to ship before we tell customers “schema v1 is stable,” otherwise we’ll keep generating support churn around inconsistent fields.
- Private parity depends on (a) event taxonomy staying stable, (b) exporter configuration changes being audited in Private, and (c) delivery semantics (at-least-once + de-dupe guidance) being documented.

Gates I propose for “launch” (i.e., we can say 100% coverage for sensitive actions):
- PM-938 finalized list of sensitive actions + explicit acceptance criteria.
- Coverage dashboard shows expected event types vs observed = 100% for each in-scope service, for a defined verification window (see below).
- CI gate blocks merges that introduce unregistered event_type or missing required fields.
- Runbook + SLO/alerts in place for audit pipeline; known failure modes documented.
- Exceptions are tracked with expiry (time-bound waivers only).

Verification window proposal:
- Hosted/Dedicated: 7-day rolling window, minimum sample counts per event_type
- Private: per-release validation in fixtures + at least one customer “canary” confirmation if applicable

Can each of you reply with:
1) “Yes/no” on resourcing assumptions for your areas
2) Any critical dependency I missed
3) Any disagreement on gates

Attachments:
- Audit-Logging-Coverage-Plan-v0.6.pdf (draft plan w/ timelines)
- Cross-Team-Dependencies-Audit-Logging-v0.3.xlsx

Thanks,
Priya
Platform Org Sponsor
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 11:03 AM PT
Subject: Re: Platform scope + resourcing: audit logging 100% sensitive-action coverage

Agree with the workstream breakdown + gates.

On resourcing: Security Eng can commit 1.0 FTE for schema/taxonomy/lib + 1.0 FTE for exporter work through end of March. CI enforcement can be covered if we keep scope tight (lint for required fields + event_type registry only; no fancy static analysis initially).

Two things to make explicit:
1) Definition of “100% coverage” needs a crisp boundary: what counts as “sensitive,” and what is considered “equivalent action across Hosted/Dedicated/Private.” I don’t want a late-stage debate where Private is held to a different bar without an exception process.
2) Delivery semantics: we should commit to at-least-once emission to the ingestion pipeline, but we need to be clear (internally and externally) that downstream exports can duplicate on retries. That implies event_id/idempotency guidance is part of “done.”

If Naomi can lock PM-938 this week, we can treat that as the source of truth for gating.

- Marcus
Engineering (Security)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 12:18 PM PT
Subject: Re: Platform scope + resourcing: audit logging 100% sensitive-action coverage

+1 to the gates as written.

On (1) definition boundary: PM-938 is in final review now. The framing we’ll use:
- “Sensitive action” = any action that changes access (RBAC/SSO), credentials, data retention/residency, export destinations, policy/routing decisions, or Private install/upgrade/rollback/config apply.
- “100% coverage” = for each sensitive action, there is a corresponding registered event_type emitted at the system of record (service owning the mutation) with required fields (actor/target/tenant/correlation/etc.) and validation passing.

On exceptions: we should require time-bound waivers (expiry required) with a risk note. Olga, I’d like your input on how we should word that for auditors.

One request: can we add an explicit launch gate for “no P0/P1 open on missing audit coverage” (e.g., SUP-18421 class). Otherwise support will keep getting hit and we’ll be stuck making claims we can’t defend.

Naomi
Product — Security & Compliance

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 18, 2026 at 1:07 PM PT
Subject: Re: Platform scope + resourcing: audit logging 100% sensitive-action coverage

Confirmed for Private: we can commit 1.0 FTE on installer/upgrade/rollback/config events through April.

Dependencies from Private side:
- We need the final event taxonomy ASAP (so we’re not renaming event_type late). If schema v1 changes after we ship installer events, we’ll create backcompat pain for customers upgrading from older Private releases.
- Export config changes in Private are tricky: there’s UI + config file + CLI pathways. We should treat ALL of those as sensitive actions and require audit events for each pathway.
- Operator identity: we can reliably capture “operator_user” only when invoked via Console/SSO. For CLI/offline operations, we can log “operator_type=local” with hostname + installer session id (no personal PII) and strongly recommend customers run via named accounts where possible.

Timeline-wise: we can target parity for install/upgrade/rollback/config apply by end of March, and then spend April tightening tests + closing gaps surfaced by the dashboard.

Vivek
Product — Private Deployments

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 19, 2026 at 9:22 AM PT
Subject: Re: Platform scope + resourcing: audit logging 100% sensitive-action coverage

This looks good from a controls/evidence standpoint, with a few specifics to include so it’s auditable:

Evidence expectations (SOC2/ISO-aligned) that we should design for:
- Demonstrate that sensitive actions are logged (screenshots/queries + sample events) and that the schema is consistent.
- Demonstrate monitoring/alerting for audit pipeline failures (drop rate, latency) + incident response runbook.
- Demonstrate access controls around who can view/configure exports.
- Demonstrate exception handling: approvals, rationale, expiry, and closure.

For waivers: time-bound is required. Also, we should require a compensating control note (e.g., “change is behind internal admin approval; activity is also captured in X system logs”). That helps if we ever need to defend “temporarily not covered” items.

One more dependency: if we plan to claim “minimize PII,” we need redaction rules + a reviewer checklist in place (and ideally a lint for obvious leak patterns). Please ensure that’s treated as a gate and not “nice to have.”

Olga
GRC

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 19, 2026 at 3:47 PM PT
Subject: Re: Platform scope + resourcing: audit logging 100% sensitive-action coverage

Locking decisions based on replies:

Resourcing confirmed:
- Security Eng: 2.0 FTE through end of March (schema/taxonomy/lib + exporter), plus lightweight CI enforcement.
- Private: 1.0 FTE through April for installer/upgrade/rollback/config apply parity.
- Platform/Control plane/Gateway/Console staffing stays as in the attached plan; I’ll sync with the relevant team leads in staff meeting to confirm explicit named owners per service.

Launch gates (final):
1) PM-938 sensitive action list finalized + published (source of truth).
2) Schema v1 + event_type registry + validator shipped.
3) CI gate blocks unregistered event_type and missing required fields for new/modified audited paths.
4) Coverage dashboard: expected vs observed = 100% for in-scope services over verification window (7-day rolling for Hosted/Dedicated; Private per-release fixtures + one canary confirmation where possible).
5) Exporter normalizes legacy events and tags schema_version.
6) Runbooks + SLO/alerts are live for audit pipeline (drop rate + delivery latency), with on-call routing.
7) Redaction/data classification guidance shipped + reviewer checklist in place (and we add a basic lint rule for obvious secrets/PII patterns where feasible).
8) No open P0/P1 “missing audit coverage” issues at time of external comms.
9) Exceptions: time-bound waivers only, with compensating controls + expiry tracked (Linear + GRC sign-off).

Cross-team dependencies to watch (highlighting the ones that can block us):
- Console: audited admin workflows + export config changes across all pathways.
- Exporter: schema_version tagging + normalization (to reduce SIEM field drift complaints).
- Private: operator identity semantics must be documented so customers understand what they will/won’t see.

Next steps:
- Naomi: publish PM-938 final by EOW; send link here.
- Marcus: confirm event_id/idempotency + de-dupe guidance is included in schema documentation.
- Vivek: add the “multiple pathways” requirement (UI/config/CLI) to the Private checklist so we don’t miss any.
- Olga: share the waiver template language + evidence checklist bullets for the Confluence control mapping.

I’ll set a weekly 30-min leadership checkpoint until we clear gate (4).

Priya
Platform Org Sponsor
Redwood Inference
